content:
The image shows a single leaf that is largely tan/brown and desiccated, with the petiole and midrib area still retaining some greenish tissue. There are scattered yellowish-brown irregular spots/lesions on the leaf surface, and the leaf appears shriveled and dried out.

Key observations:
- Whole leaf necrosis with tan/brown coloration — characteristic of tissue death, not powdery coating
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No black sooty coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- Lesions are irregular blotches, not tip/margin dieback from a single point (less consistent with Die_Back)
- The scattered dark/brown necrotic spots with irregular margins on leaf tissue are consistent with **Anthracnose** — caused by *Colletotrichum* spp., which produces irregular brown necrotic lesions that can coalesce and cause leaf browning/shriveling
- The shriveled, tan leaf with spotty necrosis pattern matches Anthracnose symptomatology on mango leaves
